punchline: After years of failure and despair, William James decided to try acting as if he were fully responsible for his whole life.
thirty_sec: As a young man, William James failed at painting and medicine, was often ill and sank into despair. After reading the philosopher Renouvier on free will, he tried an experiment: for a while, he'd act as if he were fully responsible for everything in his life. He later became one of the founders of American psychology. Mark Manson uses the story to split fault, which looks back, from responsibility, which is about what you do now.
question: Have you ever taken charge of something that wasn't your fault? How did it turn out?
